clue.text: Same cooks keeping fish on plate in 24?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the anagram wraps round the next pieces
to cook something is to work it over, so the letters of 'Same' are rearranged

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef keeps a fish on the plate, for a dish served in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' rearranges the letters of 'Same' to MASE before 'keeping' wraps it round the fish. 24 is PISA, so the definition asks for something on a plate in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian soft cream cheese, a plateful you might be served in the Tuscan city.

clue.text: Having empty garden, some arranged ornamentation

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, so only the outer letters of 'garden' stay
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of 'some' are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone with a bare garden puts out a few ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves GN from garden; 'arranged' turns SOME into OMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden statues of little bearded figures are a familiar kind of lawn decoration.

clue.text: Troublemaker, when play opens, cut off view

parts.note: a play opens with Act One, written ACT I

indicators.note: cut off means the last letter of the word for view is removed

parts.note: a vista is a view

explanation.surface: A troublemaker in the theatre blocks the audience's view as the curtain rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' trims VISTA to VIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner who stirs things up for a cause can be seen by authorities as a troublemaker.

clue.text: First driving range includes grass to do again

parts.note: first is one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: includes means holds inside, so the informer goes into the golf word

parts.note: a tee is where a golfer drives from
a grass is an informer, a rat

explanation.surface: A golf practice ground with grass on it, visited repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer, and the driving range is the golfer's tee.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat an action is to perform it once more.

clue.text: Sat perhaps removing half of hand warmers, radiant

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, an example of a day

indicators.note: removing half of a six-letter word leaves only its first three letters

parts.note: gloves keep hands warm

explanation.surface: Someone sat about taking off half their gloves, glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing half of' cuts GLOVES to GLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorescent paint in vivid colours seems to shine, hence radiant.

clue.text: Compress muscles, as vehicle's overturned in race

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles

indicators.note: in places the turned vehicle inside the race letters

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

indicators.note: overturned means flipped, so the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle; the 's is not a letter

explanation.surface: Tense your muscles as your car flips during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' gives RAC, set 'in' TT to make TRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract a text is to summarise it, squeezing it down to essentials.

clue.text: Somebody venerated self-proclaimed criminal

parts.note: someone proclaiming themselves says I
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A revered figure turns out to be an admitted crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'I con': the criminal is announcing it himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A revered person held up as a symbol is described as an idol or figurehead.

clue.text: Assistant circulating cannot reserve table in 24?

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the letters of 'cannot' are moved about

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's army reserve

explanation.surface: An assistant going round says they cannot book a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' turns CANNOT into NNACOT. 24 is PISA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian set-cream dessert, brought to the table in the Tuscan city.

clue.text: See 26
Certainly Spanish stores affected what are consumed in 24?

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so the Spanish word wraps the next piece

parts.note: si is Spanish for yes, certainly
camp means theatrically affected

explanation.surface: Spanish shops, it seems, were hit by something people eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails are a seafood dish eaten in Italy, plural like the definition.

clue.text: Calorie-free mixer added to port that's on menu in 24?

parts.note: Riga is the Baltic port and capital of Latvia

indicators.note: calorie-free means without C, the abbreviation for calorie

parts.note: tonic is a mixer for drinks

explanation.surface: A diet mixer goes with port on the drinks list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calorie-free' drops C from TONIC, leaving TONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged tube pasta is a staple item on Italian restaurant menus.

clue.text: When rambling, spit out corn to avoid unknown grub in 24?

indicators.note: rambling means wandering, so the remaining letters are jumbled
to avoid means leave out, so the unknown letter is removed from the fodder

parts.note: n is used for an unknown number in maths

explanation.surface: Someone out walking spits out corn to avoid an odd grub.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from SPITOUTCORN as told by 'to avoid', then 'rambling' rearranges the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian dry-cured ham is food you might eat in the Tuscan city; grub is slang for food.

clue.text: Sit back disheartened with current book

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read backwards
disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reader sits back, downhearted, with a book and an electric heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle I, then 'back' reverses the two letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a New Testament book, usually just called by its short name.

clue.text: Nothing allowed to deteriorate when serving up one course in 24?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing
let means allowed
to rot is to deteriorate
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: No one may let a course go off when serving it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' reverses NIL LET ROT to make TORTELLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Small stuffed pasta rings are served as a course in Italian meals.

clue.text: European, occasionally tasting, rejected food in 24?

parts.note: a Pole is a European

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the picked letters are reversed
occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is picked

explanation.surface: A European, after the odd taste, sends the food back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' gives ATN from tasting, and 'rejected' turns it to NTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornmeal porridge is a staple dish of northern Italy.

clue.text: Overseas Test cricketer once dismissing opener on ten runs

indicators.note: dismissing the opener means losing the first letter

parts.note: Ted Dexter was an England Test cricketer and captain of the 1960s
ten is written 10, read as letters IO
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A former Test batsman abroad loses his opening partner on ten runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing opener' drops the D of DEXTER. Ted Dexter captained England at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign affairs are sometimes called external or outward-facing matters, so overseas fits as an adjective.

clue.text: Standing and texting you are in New York maybe

indicators.note: in places the texting phrase inside the place word

parts.note: New York is an example of a US state
UR is text-speak for you are

explanation.surface: Texting about one's standing in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputation or importance, as in a person of standing.

clue.text: Scruffy suit's full of butter, one portion in 24?

indicators.note: full of means holding inside, so the anagram wraps the next pieces
scruffy means messy, so the letters of suit are disordered

parts.note: the word suit; the 's is not a letter
a butter is something that butts, such as a ram
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A scruffy suit stained with butter and one portion of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruffy' rearranges the letters of 'suit' to TISU; 'full of' wraps it round the butter and one. A butter is a creature that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee-soaked Italian dessert is served as a helping in Italy.

clue.text: Fuel's back in channel, getting cheer in 24?

indicators.note: in places the turned fuel word inside the channel word

parts.note: a lane is a channel, as a shipping lane

indicators.note: back means the fuel word is read backwards

parts.note: gas is a fuel; the 's is not a letter

explanation.surface: Fuel goes back into the channel, raising a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GAS into SAG. 'Cheer' is used in its old sense of food, as in good cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered baked pasta is classic Italian fare, and cheer can mean food and drink.

clue.text: Taunt son falling in stream

indicators.note: falling in means dropping inside, so the son letter goes into the stream word

parts.note: a jet is a stream of liquid

explanation.surface: Mocking a son who has fallen into a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke or jibe made at someone's expense is a taunt.

clue.text: Beatle repeatedly the old drumming, initially out of touch

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer

indicators.note: repeatedly means the old word for the is written twice

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of drumming is taken

explanation.surface: A Beatle repeatedly drumming the old way, out of touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives YEYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idealistic and dreamy is to be naive or unrealistic, detached from reality.

clue.text: Some claim Alaskans put up fare in 24?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means read from bottom to top
some means part of, so the answer lies inside the next words

explanation.surface: Some say Alaskans claim to supply this food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses the letters hidden in 'claim Alaskans' to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cured Italian sausage is typical fare eaten in Italy.

clue.text: Seat her by completely topless place for meal

indicators.note: completely topless means every word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A waiter seats a woman by a table, in a topless restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completely topless' removes the first letter of each of 'Seat', 'her' and 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal restaurant or café is somewhere to go for food.

clue.text: Bacteria making Irish poorly in resort

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the resort word

parts.note: a spa is a resort
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: An Irish visitor falls ill with bacteria at a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: These are spiral-shaped microbes, a genus of germs; the plural matches.

clue.text: City's positive with investment

definitions.note: City's stands for city is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: an ISA is a British Individual Savings Account

explanation.surface: A city is optimistic about attracting investment.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a tax-free UK savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Stinger, with drop of malt used as new spirit

indicators.note: used as new means swapped in for N, the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a nettle is a stinging plant

indicators.note: a drop of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cocktail called the Stinger with a drop of malt as a new spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The M from 'drop of malt' replaces the N of NETTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and grit, as in 'show your mettle'.

clue.text: Copper, having supremo put inside, rings about what's dished out in 24?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
put inside means the copper and boss pieces go within the rings

parts.note: two rings are two O shapes
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a boss is a supremo

explanation.surface: A policeman, with his chief put inside, rings round for the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put inside' gives OCUBOSSO and 'about' reverses it. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Braised veal shank is a Milanese dish served up across Italy.

clue.text: Settle in spacecraft, one needing fuel in 24?

indicators.note: in places the settle word within the spacecraft

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station
to nest is to settle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Settling into a spacecraft, one astronaut needs fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty Italian vegetable soup gives food, the body's fuel, in Italy.
